articleTitle: Guard-Trace Utilization for Performance Enhancement of 5G MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: One of the essential parameters to analyze the performance of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC). This study evaluates the impact of utilizing a guard-trace on a $2 \times 2$ MIMO antenna to assess the efficiency of MIMO systems in enhancing the antenna performance. The evaluation is conducted by computing the ECC value of a $2 \times 2$ MIMO antenna, using scattering parameters as the data for the computation. To conduct the evaluation, a $2 \times 2$ fifth-generation (GG) MIMO antenna is implemented in two configurations, namely without and with guard-trace. Each antenna element is made of a rectangular patch to operate at the frequency of 3.5 GHz. The inter-element distances are examined for each configuration to investigate the effect of spacing between antenna elements to the value of ECC. The analysis results indicate that the utilization of a guard-trace on $2 \times 2$ MIMO antenna can enhance its performance by reducing the correlation value without increasing the spacing between antenna elements. In addition, it is found that the ECC values calculated based on S-parameters data are aligned and strongly correlated.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Embroidered Body Worn Antenna as EM Sensor for Radiated Emissions Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: In the design of wearable sensors, it is crucial to ensure that the sensors are positioned in close proximity to the object for optimal functionality. Therefore, it is imperative to address environmental requirements to guarantee that the sensors have effective operability. This paper deals with the feasibility of an embroidered body worn antenna usage as electromagnetic (EM) sensor for radiated emissions measurement. The performances feasibility of proposed sensor, made by silver yarns embroidered on a cotton sheet as a radiating element and groundplane, is examined by measuring the radiated emission sourced by some radio frequency (RF) devices. The measurement results demonstrate good receptions of radiated emissions at the frequencies of 2.4 GHz and 2.8 GHz from the source, indicating a promising feasibility of the proposed embroidered body worn antenna as an EM sensor. In addition, the results emphasize the significance of addressing environmental factors in the measurement configuration for optimal performance in sensor applications.

articleTitle: Integrating Open-Source VoNR in 5G SA Private Networks: An Experimental Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: With the standardization of the 5th Generation of mobile networks, private $5 G$ networks are poised to support new industry verticals significantly. For small and medium-sized companies, affordability is crucial for the adoption and deployment of these solutions. Open-source projects that implement components of the 5 G system are likely to play a key role in reducing the entry barrier for private $\mathbf{5 G}$ network solutions. This research paper presents the world’s first voice-over-5G prototype using only open-source projects, successfully implemented at Technische Universität Berlin, along with initial performance measurements.

articleTitle: Introducing Secure Element Token With USB Wi-Fi Bluetooth Triple Communication Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative secure element token, which supports three communication interfaces, USB, WiFi, and Bluetooth. The token is built with a system on chip (SoC) module including FLASH memory, and a secure element (javacard) with a mini SIM form factor. The secure element is managed via ISO7816 five wires interface, thanks to an original library. We present use cases for each communication interface. Serial USB is used to upload software in the SoC, and thereafter to download javacard application in secure element according to Global Platform (GP) protocols. Wi-Fi enables internet access to secure element thanks to TLS1.3 server running within secure element. Bluetooth allows interactions with mobile applications, such as Bluetooth terminal, which use the SoC to build Ethereum transactions signed by secure element.

articleTitle: Automated Validation of Spatial Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Spatial databases, are often based on relational database management systems (RDBMS), to incorporate geographical data essential for data planning and optimization. However, maintaining the integrity of spatial data poses challenges, particularly in enforcing topological rules and preventing performance degradation during query execution. In this context, we propose an automated geometry validation application tailored for database environments, complemented by a user-friendly web-based interface. Our solution addresses the issue of invalid geometries often encountered in datasets, enhancing the reliability and efficiency of spatial database operations. Through performance and accuracy evaluations, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving the overall user experience and trust in data planning processes with minimal implementation efforts.

articleTitle: Social Robots in Education: To Select or Not to Select a Robot for a Teaching Subject at an Educational Level?
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Social robots have been widely adopted in all levels of education for teaching multiple subjects, due to their reported potential to motivate and support learning outcomes. The goal of this work is to systematically research the literature and gather information relative to social robot applications for educational purposes. Subsequently, these applications are classified by educational level and by subject, aiming to investigate which robots are chosen in each case. Five educational levels are defined (preschool, primary, secondary, higher, and lifelong education), 23 teaching subjects, and 50 robots. Results indicate Primary education as the educational level mainly adapting social robots to support teaching courses, language and science courses as the most popular subjects, while NAO and Pepper as the robots mostly used. Results also indicate that the selection of the social robot in each case is not based on a structured scientific approach depending on the level and subject of education. The latter highlights that there is a need to further investigate the appropriate selection process of social robots for specific courses and educational levels, taking into account their future potential to contribute to education, especially considering their already documented contribution without following any specific selection protocol.

articleTitle: Analyzing Reading Patterns with Webcams: An Eye-Tracking Study of the Albanian Language
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Eye-tracking technologies have proven to be an important tool for understanding human behaviour. Unfortunately, high quality eye-tracking devices are not always affordable, especially in the case of studying low-resource languages. In this study we aim to explore the usage of low-cost opportunities, such as the usage of the WebGazer JavaScript library, utilizing normal webcams, to study an under resourced language such as Albanian. We present a study of the reading patterns in Albanian, with a primary aim to enlarge available datasets in our language and evaluate the accuracy and trustworthiness of the WebGazer library in capturing reading patterns. Our results demonstrate that the usage of webcams is an effective solution in the case where high-cost devices are not available. Various limitations in the webcam technology indicate the necessity to make further improvements in webcam eye-tracking models.

articleTitle: Determination of the Impact of Video Encoding Parameters on QoE Using Passive Viewing Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Optimizing video encoding parameters is essential for cloud gaming service providers to deliver high-quality gaming experiences to their users. In this study, we conducted a passive Quality of Experience testing on a publicly available dataset of cloud gaming sessions to evaluate the impact of video encoding parameters on the Quality of Experience ratings of the samples. Participants assessed the quality of video streams utilizing a selected methodology, and statistical analysis was conducted to ascertain how various parameters affected the average quality ratings of diverse game genres. We further investigated the impact of quality settings on the participants’ willingness to play. Additionally, we explored the applicability of passive viewing tests by comparing our QoE analysis results with previous research that used active viewing tests in cloud gaming evaluations.

articleTitle: Cell Stay Time Characteristics Exploration in Beyond 5G Small Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Cell Stay Time (CST) is the cornerstone for numerous new applications in new-generation networks such as mobility prediction, resource reservation strategy, handover prediction, and more. In the era of the current 5G and toward 6 G in the future, when these mentioned applications will become the key solutions to advance a smarter and automatic network system, CST’s role will undoubtedly become more and more crucial, and this leads to the demand of study it to understand and use it properly. Unfortunately, there is a lack of research focused on this problem. Realizing its importance, in this topic, we investigate several important characteristics of CST in terms of distribution, means, and variance relationship according to the change of the cell’s radius in the case of smaller cells. This topic aims to contribute a deeper view of CST, which can become materials for researchers to study and apply in their future work.

articleTitle: ML Classification of BLE Packets Using Restrain Receiver QoS Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The pervasiveness of technology in people’s lives is creating real difficulties for wireless protocols to cope with the constant increase in communications. Avoidance mechanisms exist, but they are no longer robust enough to limit collisions. A renewal of countermeasure techniques is needed to optimise spectrum management in a dynamic spectral context. In this paper, we propose an improvement of the radio receiver AGC computation based on machine learning (ML). We studied four ML algorithms for classifying BLE packets interfered by Wi-Fi: Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), bagged tree (BT), and random subspace using KNN. The analysis suggests that the receiver can use signal quality metrics (RSSI, SNR, LQI) to classify packets, to determined an optimized AGC index and to detect non-ideal reception conditions.

articleTitle: Comparative Machine Learning Analysis of PM2.5 and PM10 Forecasting in Albania
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Air pollution continues to be a critical health risk factor for populations worldwide. Tirana, the capital city of Albania with a high population density, confronts significant environmental challenges, particularly concerning air quality, which are being increasingly assessed Internet of Things (IoT) technologies and sensors. Previous research has utilized IoT system to gather air quality time series data (particulate matters, temperature, humidity, air pressure) during 24 - 28 September 2019 and using only random forest regression model for predictions of each parameter. This paper extends the research by conducting a comprehensive comparative analysis of four machine learning models, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Random Forest Regression (RFR), Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR), and Support Vector Regression (SVR), to predict particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10) levels. The novelty of this study lies in its multi-model approach, using the same dataset with six attributes, to determine the most effective model for air quality forecasting. Evaluation metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), and R-squared score are utilized to assess the models’ performance. The results demonstrate that the Random Forest model outperforms others in terms of accuracy and efficiency, providing a robust solution for air quality prediction in urban settings.

articleTitle: Spherical Human Phantoms for Characterization of Implanted Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Implantable antennas cannot be characterized by methods suitable for standard antennas because they are embedded in lossy human tissue, which affects the antenna parameters. In this paper, we consider a canonical spherical human phantom which allows us to characterize the implanted antennas and to determine parameters such as the total radiated power, the power density reaching free space and the antenna gain. For all the mentioned parameters, simple analytical formulas have been derived that enable the calculation of the initial communication link budget between the implanted antenna and an access point located either on the surface body or in the environment out of the body. The results of these expressions have been compared to rigorous models showing excellent agreement and providing valuable insights.

articleTitle: Growth Plate Area Segmentation on Knee MRIs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The application of artificial intelligence plays a crucial role in modern medicine, helping to improve diagnostic process and patient care. This paper aims to explore the segmentation process on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of knee joint to segment the age-related parts of the knee joint, which are not sufficiently studied in age assessment research of young individuals. This paper presents and analyzes the results of MRI segmentation of the knee obtained using U-Net and U-net++ neural networks. Both networks were trained from scratch on a private dataset consisting of 530 2D knee MRI images. U-Net achieves a mean dice similarity coefficient value of 0.9415 and a mean Jaccardi index value of 0.8949 for knee bone segmentation, compared to U-Net++ with a mean dice similarity coefficient of 0.9280 and a mean Jaccardi index value of 0.8747.

articleTitle: Framework for Integrating Threat Modeling into a DevOps Pipeline for Enhanced Software Development
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: In the realm of continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD), safeguarding software systems is crucial. Integrating threat modeling into the DevOps pipeline ensures that security considerations are an integral part of the software development process, helping to prevent vulnerabilities from being introduced into production. This study outlines a detailed framework for embedding threat modeling into a Jenkins DevOps pipeline. The framework involves incorporating threat model results into a database and using this data to perform automated security scans. Three challenges are identified in integration of security in DevOps pipeline and discussed against the proposed framework.

articleTitle: A Note on the Use of Hybrid Numerical Method Approach in Dosimetry for Exposure to mmWaves
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The paper deals with the assessment of the absorbed power denisty (APD) in a spherical head model using FEKO simulation tool and the Gauss-Legendre quadrature. A hybrid approach featuring the use of Method of Moments (MoM) and Finite Element Method (FEM) with a Multi-Level Fast Multiple Method (MLFMM) to accelerate the computation, has been chosen to compare with the related results in literature obtained using other numerical approaches. Here the numerical results are obtained using some modifications of the spherical head model, such as hemisphere and hemispherical shell, within the limited computational capabilities, giving the distributions of electric and magnetic fields and the APD calculated on the control surface. The discrepancies with the reported results obtained with other simulation tools (CST, HFSS) have been studied.

articleTitle: Combined EFIE-EFIE Formulation for PEC and Penetrable Object: Study of Reduced Planar Model Exposed to Dipole Antenna Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The paper is on the use of an integral equation based formulation in high frequency dosimetry. The analysis is carried out on the use of a reduced planar models, exposed to radiation of dipole antenna positioned at various distances to planar model. The antenna is modeled as a thin equivalent strip based on the electric field integral equation (EFIE) formulation for perfect electrically conducting (PEC) body. The reduced planar body model is based on the EFIE formulation for the penetrable (dielectric) body. Both combined problems are solved by a method of moments (MoM) approach. The electric field determined from the EFIE-PEC part is utilized as input to the EFIE-dielectric part of the proposed model. The numerical results for the equivalent surface currents, and the induced electric field on reduced planar model surface are given. Also, the analysis of several electric field measures obtained at the averaging surface is carried out to assess the effects of different dipole positions when reduced models of varying thickness and width are used.

articleTitle: Assessment of Current Flowing through the Human Body in a Case of Fault Current
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The paper deals with an assessment of the maximum permissible current through the human body when standing above a horizontally buried grounding electrode into which fault current is injected. The analysis is based on the thin wire antenna theory and the Pocklington integral equation handled via the Galerkin Bubnov indirect boundary element method (GB-IBEM). Provided the step voltage is determined, a simplified model of the human body is used to estimate the current that flows through a person from one foot to the other. The study considers both scenarios: when the individual is barefooted and when wearing protective shoes.

articleTitle: Advancing Quantum Communications: Q-OFDM with Quantum Fourier Transforms for Enhanced Signal Integrity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The integration of Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiplexing (OFDM) with contemporary communication systems faces challenges, notably the requirement of a cyclic prefix (CP), which affects spectral efficiency. This paper proposes a novel quantum OFDM transmission method that utilizes quantum mechanisms for encoding, decoding, and channel processes, replacing the need for Discrete Fourier Transforms (DFT) and Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform (IDFT). This advanced quantum OFDM model eliminates the CP requirement and, when compared to a standard quantum transmission scheme, shows improved accuracy in quantum state measurement, especially in channels with higher resistivity. The results have been validated using simulations on IBM’s Qiskit platform.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Autonomous Vehicle Behavior With Imbalanced & Mixed Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Autonomous vehicles are equipped with proprietary Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology, which is confidential and inaccessible. To ensure its operational integrity predective models are used. These models integrate numerous data sources and machine learning techniques to enhance the vehicle’s ability to navigate, recognize objects, and avoid obstacles safely and efficiently. Before being marketed in Europe, vehicles undergo a series of tests conducted in diffrentes scenarios. When the decision made by vehicle corresponds to a safe situation, the test result is considered as OK. Otherwise, it is KO. Hence, this can be seen as a classification problem and can be modeled by implementing a classifiers trained on observed data. However, it has been observed that datasets contain imbalanced data, with a higher number of OK tests compared to KO trials. To implement the classifier effectively, this imbalance must be addressed. Various solutions from the literature, including resampling techniques like SMOTE and its variants adapted for mixed data, can help. This study aims to apply these methods to a real dataset derived from vehicle tests incorporating AI. The SMOTE-ENC variant has demonstrated its effectiveness, particularly in classifying the positive KO class, correctly identifying 5 out of 6 tests. In contrast, the non-rebalanced approach misclassifies 5 out of 6 tests.

articleTitle: Stochastic Analysis in MIMO and Passive Antenna Electric Field Calculation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: This paper presents the sequel on previous author’s work and deals with the stochastic analysis of electric field calculation procedures in the vicinity of base station antenna emphasizing the effect of MIMO antenna system mostly used in new 5G technology. Electric field is calculated considering three different approaches: Free Space model (FS), Perfect Ground Reflection model (PG), and Fresnel’s plane wave approximation model (FRM). The reflection occurs over two-layered soil (medium) described with relative permittivity and electric conductivity of each layer, as well as with the thickness of the upper layer. The uncertainty quantification (UQ) is derived using Monte Carlo (MC) stochastic method. Stochastic mean and double standard deviation of the output are computed and sensitivity analysis (SA) is carried out in order to analyze the level of impact of input parameters’ variations on the resulting electric field.

articleTitle: Time Domain Study of Wireless Power Transfer Between Coupled Dipoles Above a Half-Space
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The paper deals with a measure for power transfer efficiency (PTE) expressed as a ratio of squared root-mean values (RMS) of current at the input of received and transmitted wire antenna, respectively, placed above a half-space. The measures arise from direct time domain analysis of wire antennas of finite length. The space-time dependent currents along the wires, as a basis of time domain analysis, are obtained by numerically solving the corresponding set of coupled Hallen integral equations. Knowing the space-time distribution of current and charge along dipoles, time domain (TD) energy measures and corresponding PTE measure are computed.

articleTitle: GNSS Spoofing Attack in Real-time Static and Dynamic Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) spoofing attacks are a current topic in the GNSS community due to their frequencies and ease of execution. Therefore, it is necessary to detect them promptly and to test and analyze the behavior of different receivers and signal observables in different conditions under these attacks. In this paper, spoofing attacks experiments on different devices are performed in two outdoor scenarios: static and dynamic. The analysis and comparison of different GNSS signal observables of both scenarios are derived to detect fake signals. This research aims to analyze the obtained distributions of observables’ samples based on the obtained results and to monitor the behavior of different observables in both scenarios for reliable spoofing detection. Our experimental results show similar and expected observables’ behavior in both scenarios except the pseudorange. In both scenarios, the location, date, and time of all used receivers are successfully spoofed. The navigation system of smartphone with Android operating system version 14 is taken over by the spoofer, which indicates the vulnerability of new generation smartphones.

articleTitle: Analytical Approach to the Assessment of the Step Voltage at the Surface Above the Horizontal Grounding Electrode
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The paper deals with the analytical approach to the assessment of step voltage for the case of horizontal grounding electrode energized by the ideal current source due to the fault or lightning channel current, respectively. The analytical solution of homogenous Pocklington equation provides the current distribution along the electrode in a closed form and, consequently, calculation of the voltage distribution in the vicinity of the electrode from the telegrapher’s equation via numerical integration. Finally, a straightforward calculation of step voltage is carried out. Some illustrative results for the current along the electrode and step voltage are given.

articleTitle: A Cloud-Based Software Architecture for a Course Recommender System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Main contribution of the paper is to design cloud architecture and validate that architecture via real example in university recommendation system. Paper investigates state of the art, goes briefly trough analysis and design process, continues with development and validation of the architecture and the results from the experiments. The architecture was developed with the idea of meeting the need for a high-performance and scalable recommender system, which eliminates the need to purchase and maintain expensive servers with large computing power. Additionally, a dataset for training the course recommendation model, sourced from the extensive data available on the Coursera platform, was created.

articleTitle: Securing Primary Users in IoT 5G Cognitive Radio Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has transformed device communication, necessitating reliable information security, especially physical layer security (PLS). Protecting data confidentiality in wireless transfers is critical in IoT environments. Cognitive Radio Networks (CRNs) optimize spectrum utilization, enhancing network efficiency. This study investigates PLS in CRNs, featuring a primary source-destination pair and a secondary user (SU) that performs cooperative jamming to secure the primary user’s (PU) communication. The SU generates artificial interference, with transmit power determined by the primary network’s interference tolerance. We develop mathematical formulas to assess outage probabilities, aiming to enhance security and efficiency in IoT and spectrum management.

articleTitle: Classification of Power-Grid Signal Transients based on Matched Filters and Graph Signal Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a technique for detecting and classifying transients within an electrical signal. Our approach uses the standard matched filter for transient detection and employs graph signal processing and cross-correlation for transient classification. In this way, a more precise analysis of the condition of the power system can be made. The results indicate that this method effectively identifies various types of transients and proficiently categorizes them, also addressing cases where transient classes are not well defined. Furthermore, our procedure exhibits robustness to changes in criteria, offering potential benefits for real signal analysis. To facilitate comprehension, the approach is presented through a detailed, step-by-step example.

articleTitle: Measurements of Frequency Splitting Phenomenon in Resonant Wireless Power Transfer System of Inductively Fed Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: In this paper, we observe the frequency splitting phenomenon in four-coil resonant wireless power transfer systems. First, a simple approach for easy setup of the inductively fed antennas in the mode of the resonant transformer is proposed. Then, the system is simulated in 4 nec 2 software, manufactured, and finally set and measured by a vector network analyzer. An experiment with wireless light is shown for the illustration.

articleTitle: A New Look to the Maxwell’s Equations and Wave Equations in Conducting Media
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: This paper presents a new system of Maxwell’s equations and wave equations in conducting media containing electromagnetic field sources, where the sources of the static component of the electric field are electric current sources, rather than electric charges. Maxwell’s third differential equation is derived from Maxwell’s first differential equation, resulting in a new form of Maxwell’s third differential equation specific to conducting media. This new equation differs from Maxwell’s third differential equation in perfect dielectrics (Gauss’s law). Gauss’s law is valid in a conducting medium only if it is a linear and isotropic source-free conducting medium. The volume density of the source (impressed) electric current in conducting media is introduced as a novel physical quantity, analogous to the volume density of the electric charge in perfect dielectrics.

articleTitle: Machine Learning and Dynamic Time Warping for Online Signature Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Signature verification is a very common task in the field of document analysis used for the identification and validation of individuals. Many approaches can be used for signature classification. Using a machine-learning-based system is one of the most common approaches. This paper uses machine learning to classify signatures as genuine or forged. It also used a dynamic time-warping approach in the preprocessing step to produce data for training purposes. This approach differs from using it in the classification phase, which is a common practice in signature verification. The work targets online signatures, which are obtained using digital devices. Different databases were used to evaluate the accuracy of the verification systems, and four different algorithms were used for classification. The results are very promising. The minimum error rate achieved was 2.09% for the MCYT-100 dataset, 3.34% for the SVC2004 dataset, $\mathbf{1. 6 8 \%}$ for the SigComp’11-Chinese dataset, and $\mathbf{3. 6 8 \%}$ for the SigComp’11- Dutch dataset.

articleTitle: A Digital Watermark Architecture for Image Authentication Based on Hermite Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The paper introduces an invisible image watermarking approach using a binary image as a watermark in combination with the Hermite transform. By using the secret key, the binary watermark is separated into several partial binary images before being embedded into the transform domain coefficients. Embedding is done into several bit planes of the Hermite coefficients to ensure invisibility and robustness. The Hermite transform proves to be efficient in diverse applications and outperforms traditional approaches, especially in block-based image processing. Namely, it is shown that the Hermite transform can be used for image deblocking to mitigate the impact of ringing artifacts and blurring introduced by using the Fourier or discrete cosine transform-based approaches. Our focus is on defining a low-complexity architecture for real-time Hermite-based image watermarking. Therefore, the procedure is adopted to work in a vector manner to facilitate the hardware implementation. The schematic depiction of the design is provided and the complexity is discussed.

articleTitle: UWB Channel Impulse Response Alignment Techniques for Accurate Indoor Radio Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: A framework for the cost-effective, robust, and ubiquitous acquisition of hyper-reliable channel information encapsulated in channel impulse response (CIR) and other channel parameters relevant to diverse usage scenarios is one of the essential requirements for radio sensing. Due to its good temporal resolution, ultra-wideband (UWB) technology is promising to be included in the acquisition framework. The accuracy of the CIR estimated with commercially available UWB radios has to be comprehensively evaluated to satisfy the requirement for hyperreliable channel data. In this paper, we address the alignment problem of measured UWB CIRs that affects the accuracy of the final channel information provided for radio sensing. Correlation-based processing techniques for CIR alignment in the time domain are proposed as alternatives to the techniques based on the arrival time of the first multipath component provided by proprietary algorithms. Measurement campaigns using commercial IEEE 802.15.4 compliant radios and vector network analyzer (VNA) carried out in office and laboratory indoor environments confirm the validity of the correlation-based alignment techniques.

articleTitle: Launch Power Control for Digital Subcarrier Equalization in Filterless Optical Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: This paper investigates the advantages of exploiting launch power control in point-to-multipoint (P2MP) transceivers when deployed in filterless horseshoe optical networks. In order to realize simple and cost-effective optical nodes, 2-by-2 optical couplers can be used in these networks, resulting in a filterless architecture that avoids the deployment of expensive wavelength selective switches (WSSs). Optical amplifiers can be deployed as needed to compensate for losses. However, if P2MP transceivers are used, in the upstream direction the receiver can only tolerate up to a certain difference between the power levels of the incoming signals. Meeting this limit may demand additional amplifiers to be used in the transmission paths. Leveraging the ability to control the launch power of each transmitter in the upstream direction can mitigate the need to deploy additional amplifiers. This work proposes a mathematical framework to minimize the number of optical amplifiers required in filterless horseshoe networks fitted with P2MP transceivers with launch power control. The results support the benefits of having launch power control in the transceivers to reduce the number of optical amplifiers required when exploiting $\mathbf{P} 2 \mathrm{MP}$ connectivity in the optical domain.

articleTitle: Anycast Metrics and Performance Tuning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Anycast has wide adoption in global network services such as Domain Name Service (DNS) and Content Delivery Networks (CDN). Its performance is determined by the location of client terminal, the anycast service points of presence (PoP), as well as network routing and conditions. The performance can be measured using various metrics such as latency and load balancing. The question arises what are the most useful metrics to evaluate anycast performance, and whether the operator can do anything to improve it. In this paper we define three performance metrics for anycast deployments, and propose several practical BGP configuration steps an operator can take to improve the metrics. Using these steps we show a significant improvement of anycast performance in our test deployment in Europe and the USA.

articleTitle: Smart Street Lighting for Enhancing Energy Efficiency in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of urban development, innovative solutions are constantly sought to improve the quality of life of residents. Moving away from conventional static street lighting, one such transformative solution for residential environments is smart street lighting. This intelligent solution brings an increase in energy efficiency. In this paper, the goal is to analyze the implementation of smart street lighting within the concept of a smart city based on the possibilities of saving and efficient use of energy. In selected case studies of urban scenarios, through simulation procedures, the possibility of implementing smart lighting was analyzed from the point of view of energy saving, indicating the importance of this aspect in the context of building smart energy lighting systems in urban environments. The discussions given in the paper show a quantitative assessment of energy savings in urban areas by replacing traditional lighting systems. The results of the analyzes show that the analyzed solutions provide useful guidelines for the application of the concept of smart lighting in urban environments and the selection of suitable solutions with regard to possible reductions in energy costs.

articleTitle: Deploying Testbed Docker-based application for Encryption as a Service in Kubernetes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The scalability of today’s networking infrastructures, such as Kubernetes, has increased the demand for everything-as-a-service concepts, including encryption services. This paper details deploying an Encryption as a Service (EaaS) framework on Kubernetes. In our current implementation, a web platform is dedicated to the subscription processes and managing the requested services. Service providers subscribe to receive encryption and decryption services for their clients, and a token is assigned to them. The client, or better to say, the devices covered by that service provider, can use encryption/decryption to specify that token. As our implemented web platform is written in Django, through this paper, we have discussed the deployment of Django applications on Kubernetes and the role of two other services (i.e., Database and Nginx) to make it available. The services are executed on Docker containers and deployed on Kubernetes pods. We have also explained the steps to build Docker containers, including the details of Dockerfiles. We have deployed this framework on both local and remote Kubernetes environments. The former deployment was performed by setting up a local Minikube cluster, while the latter assumes a remote Kubernetes cluster, and we are connecting to it through a VPN. We have tested the availability and accuracy of the encryption/decryption services and checked the logs to ensure that these services work correctly. We aim to present this article to assist researchers wishing to conduct effective testing or a Testbed in the real world.

articleTitle: Adaptive Resource Management in Software-Defined Networks for IoT Ecosystems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has imposed some challenges on traditional network management systems, necessitating diverse approaches for efficient resource allocation. In this paper, we present a framework for adaptive resource management in Software-Defined Networks (SDNs) tailored to IoT ecosystems. Leveraging the inherent flexibility and programmability of SDNs, our methodology integrates reinforcement learning techniques to dynamically allocate network resources based on real-time demands of IoT applications. Our approach introduces a dual-stage Deep Q-Network (DQN) architecture, enhancing stability and accuracy in learning optimal resource allocation policies. This dual-stage DQN, combined with a multi-agent reinforcement learning strategy, maximizes network performance while ensuring fairness and Quality of Service (QoS). The proposed system is evaluated in a simulated IoT environment using the OpenDaylight (ODL) SDN controller. The experimental results demonstrate a significant improvement in key performance metrics, including increased throughput, reduced latency, and decreased energy consumption compared to traditional methods. These enhancements highlight the potential of our adaptive resource management framework in addressing the complex requirements of modern IoT ecosystems.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Prediction of Power Usage Effectiveness: A Machine Learning Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a comprehensive six-month case study on the operations of an IT company’s data center. Environmental and operational parameters such as temperature, humidity, voltage, energy consumption, and power readings were meticulously collected. The Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) metric was derived using real-time data on consumed versus total available energy. We applied machine learning models, including Support Vector Machine (SVM), Linear Regression, and Random Forest, to predict the PUE metric. Each model’s performance was evaluated using metrics such as Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE). The results demonstrated that the Random Forest model outperformed the other models, indicating its potential as an effective tool for predicting data center energy efficiency. This paper is important as it provides actionable insights and a data-driven approach to improving energy efficiency in data centers, which is critical for reducing operational costs and minimizing environmental impact.

articleTitle: Heuristic Malware Detection Method Based on Structured CTI Data: A Research Study and Proposal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: This article addresses the significant and evolving threat of malware, particularly ransomware, to critical infrastructure sectors such as energy, banking, and food supply. Traditional detection methods that rely on specific indicators of compromise, like file hashes or IP addresses, can be easily circumvented by attackers. This paper presents a novel heuristic approach to malware detection using structured cyber threat intelligence data. By aggregating high-level indicators of compromise such as file modifications, registry key changes, and suspicious network communications, this method aims to identify malicious patterns indicative of malware behavior. The proposed detection system employs advanced machine learning techniques, including graph neural networks, to analyze these aggregated indicators of compromise. This approach enables earlier detection of malware, reduces the mean time to detect breaches, and minimizes false positives. The system utilizes the STIX data format for improved interoperability and analysis of cyber threat intelligence data.

articleTitle: Network Traffic Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The paper explores the application of machine learning algorithms for network traffic intrusion detection with the aim of enhancing the security of information systems. More specifically, it provides a comprehensive insight into the current state of the art in intrusion detection, and gives a review of relevant literature, research methodology, implementation of various machine learning models, and analysis of the obtained results. Our findings indicate the outstanding potential of models, such as decision trees, in identifying malicious activities, offering valuable guidance for the development of more efficient systems for network security.

articleTitle: Automated Data Correlation for IoT Anomaly Detection with B5G Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Smart city monitoring technologies, including IoT devices like sensors and smart cameras, enable real-time anomaly detection by analyzing data from various locations. While video and audio can identify unsafe activities, camera coverage is limited, necessitating audio detectors for out-of-sight incidents. Static methods do not perform well under conditions like low-quality voice due to illness or mood, highlighting the need for a dynamic mechanism to orchestrate data collection, clean background noise, correlate data, and identify public safety incidents. This paper addresses challenges in correlating data from IoT devices at different locations, orchestrating information among various IoT service providers, and ensuring communication between IoT and network domains. The proposed architecture leverages AI to analyze IoT data in real-time for automatic anomaly detection, making it well-suited for AI-enabled Beyond 5G (B5G) networks. Analysis results are sent to operators via orchestrators to pinpoint the location of anomalous IoT devices. This information is also relayed to public safety agencies for appropriate action. Unlike existing systems focused on audio and video data, the proposed architecture can be applied to any IoT data, enhancing monitoring and detection capabilities.

articleTitle: SyncNet: Harmonizing Nodes for Efficient Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: This research investigates a novel communication-efficient algorithm, SyncNet, for training large neural networks on massive datasets. The ever-growing size of datasets necessitates distributing the training workload across vast machine networks, often containing many machines. While economically feasible, such large-scale training suffers from limitations like communication overhead associated with gradient transmission and increased vulnerability to network failures. SyncNet addresses these limitations by employing a remarkably simple approach. Nodes in the network transmit only the sign (positive or negative) of their gradient vector to a central server. This server then aggregates these signs using a majority vote to determine the overall update direction for the model parameters. Compared to traditional full-precision distributed SGD, SyncNet demonstrates approximately a 25 percent reduction in per iteration time. The research establishes theoretical convergence, which guarantees for SyncNet in both large-scale and mini-batch settings under realistic conditions verified through experimentation.

articleTitle: Advancing Healthcare 5.0 through Federated Learning: Opportunity for Security Enforcement using Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: As Healthcare 5.0 becomes more widely accepted, the healthcare industry in general is changing, leading to better patient care and more system efficiency. The degree of digital automation that introduced cutting-edge technology applications to the health sector is seriously challenged by this shift. Concerns over patient’s privacy and security are heightened by the rising digitization of healthcare institutions, which makes it harder to collaborate and share data seamlessly. The exponential growth of healthcare data necessitates effective processing and analysis in order to maximize patient outcomes and healthcare delivery. To fully realize the potential of Healthcare 5.0, healthcare practitioners, information technology specialists, data scientists, and researchers must address these complex security difficulties. Healthcare 5.0 provides a comprehensive solution to the pressing issues facing the digitalized healthcare industry by thoroughly examining its foundational principles and exploring its practical implementation through cloud computing, data analytics, and federated learning. Through healthcare federated learning, the national electronic health (e-health) policy and strategy will be legitimized. In this paper, the authors categorized and combined healthcare technology with federated learning artificial intelligence (AI) at various automation stages. The paper discussed the issues that are now facing the healthcare industry, such as security, privacy and dependability. The paper provided readers with guidance on how to use AI and federated learning to solve healthcare information system synchronization. In conclusion, the authors discussed broad security topics and future research in the healthcare management system utilizing federated learning and blockchain approach.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning in Building Neural Network Model Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The transfer learning approach to the development of deep learning (DL) models accelerates the solving of the set task. It also allows solving tasks when large data sets required for extracting non-linear mapping functions are not available. This approach can even reduce the need for large computer resources. This paper contains a case study that shows how easily and quickly it is possible to build a DL model on sparse data using a transfer learning approach. Image processing task was chosen because the development of convolutional neural networks (CNN-Convolutional Neural Network) has led to excellent results in solving the challenges of image classification and object localization and detection. The transfer learning approach enabled simplified and accelerated model development for the selected task. The applied process is formalized into separate distinct procedural steps. A system for the automatic detection of Alzheimer’s dementia through MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) images was the task that needed to be solved. The popular CNN AlexNet architecture was used as a starting point for the development of the new model. A minimally modified model developed by transfer learning achieved an average accuracy of over 88% and an average recall of over 91%. These results are quite comparable to human operators.

articleTitle: Adaptive Compressive Sensing Image Recovery Using Block-Variance-Based Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The paper proposes an adaptive sampling and reconstruction procedure for image denoising, exploiting the variance of image blocks to distinguish between flat and busy regions. This classification is used to make a decision on the number of samples to discard from each block: more samples can be discarded in flat regions compared to busy ones. This optimizes the denoising process while preserving block quality. Additionally, an image fusion technique is applied to enhance the quality of the reconstructed/denoised image. The procedure is iteratively repeated. It is tested on several images corrupted by Gaussian noise. The proposed approach is compared with a conventional non-adaptive sampling for image denoising and reconstruction and a $3 \times 3$ mean filtering approach. The results show PSNR improvement for all considered cases.

articleTitle: Out of Distribution Generalization: KPI vs Spectrogram Based Jamming Classification in 5G
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Nowadays, 5G network deployments and use cases increasingly rely on Artificial Intelligence to enhance network security. Machine Learning models can be leveraged to detect and classify attacks on the network-such as jamming-using Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) like SINR, MCS, and CQI as training data. Another prevalent method involves using spectrograms as training data, effectively transforming the task into an image classification challenge. In dynamic environments like 5G, encompassing every possible scenario when collecting training data is impractical. Hence, it’s crucial to develop resilient models that maintain high accuracy when exposed to data of a different distribution in the real world-a concept known as Out-of-Distribution (OOD) Generalization. This study compares the accuracy and resilience of models created using these two methodologies. Initially, models were evaluated using their respective hold-out datasets, and later with OOD test data incorporating first attenuated 5 G signals data and then diverse traffic types data. Our results show that spectrogram-based models achieved 100% accuracy on respective hold-out datasets, lowest of 96% on different traffic type OOD test data, and lowest of 66% on attenuated OOD test data. In contrast, the best-performing KPI-based model reached a maximum of 92% on its respective hold-out dataset but showed poor performance on OOD test sets, at times misclassifying everything. We thus infer that spectrogram-based models exhibit superior accuracy and resilience in 5G jamming detection and classification.

articleTitle: Robust DNN-Enabled Cooperative Spectrum Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: In this contribution, we investigate cooperative spectrum sensing in cognitive radio networks using a deep neural network approach. Our proposed architecture leverages the strengths of both a one dimentional convolutional neural network and a bidirectional long short-term memory network. This combined approach aims to effectively learn the activity patterns of primary users for accurate spectrum sensing. The signal generation process incorporates diverse modulation techniques commonly used in communication systems. Additionally, the channel model considers complexities encountered in real-world deployments. These complexities mimic the challenges of multipath propagation and relative motion, making the training data more realistic. The performance of the proposed deep neural network is compared to benchmark methods using only CNN or LSTM at the secondary user level. We evaluate the models using receiver operating characteristic curves and probability of detection for various signal-to-noise ratio levels. The simulation results showcase the effectiveness of the proposed DNN, achieving superior probability of detection compared to the benchmarks and potentially surpassing state-of-the-art methods, particularly demonstrating very good performance at very low SNR values.

articleTitle: Unraveling the Potential of AI Towards Digital and Green Transformation in Kiwifruit Farming
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Growing awareness of the population of health benefits related to kiwifruit consumption, led to its increased market demand. As demands grow, producers need efficient and sustainable practices to provide enhanced outputs, in terms of yield quality and quantity, by optimally managing their inputs, in terms of resources. To achieve the latter goals, digitalization and precision operations of farming practices introduced Precision Agriculture (PA). PA have harnessed the potential of technological improvements to revolutionize kiwifruit industry. To this end, in this work, a narrative review is conducted to gather information and add to existing research on PA of kiwifruit. Research findings are analyzed and interpreted towards allowing readers to capture the broad range of current status and perspective of AI in kiwifruit farming. Results indicate a lack of public datasets, and limited multi-modal data fusion techniques; AI-based robotic automation for harvesting and pollination is reported, while automation for weeding, pruning and spraying has not yet been developed, leaving space for more innovations towards the overall digital and green transformation of the kiwifruit industry.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Risk Management of Generative AI based Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: This paper addresses cybersecurity challenges in integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into applications. It proposes a risk analysis approach that focuses on identifying threats and vulnerabilities exploited by malicious actors, which is validated through a case study on prompt injection attacks. The results demonstrated the efficacy of our approach in identifying and quantifying vulnerabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs).

articleTitle: Supporting Academic Teaching with Integrating AI in Learning Management Systems: Introducing a Toolchain for Students and Lecturers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming educational technology by enhancing both teaching and learning processes. This paper examines the “LearnStreamAI” project at Technikum Wien, which integrates an AI-driven chatbot within the Moodle LMS to support real-time student interactions. Utilizing advanced AI technologies like OpenAI’s ChatGPT-4, Google Gemini, and Anthropic Claude3, the chatbot adapts to individual students’ knowledge levels, provides tailored feedback, and enhances engagement through interactive elements in quizzes. Multilingual subtitles using OpenAI’s Whisper technology further improve accessibility for diverse student bodies. In parallel, a toolchain has been developed that automates the creation of academic materials using a PowerShell script and the OpenAI API, based on an easily maintainable Excel input file. This includes generating PowerPoint slides, Moodlecompatible questions, and detailed topic descriptions, all exported into Moodle XML format. The approach ensures accessibility and ease of use for lecturers across various disciplines. The results indicate significant time savings and improved consistency in material preparation. Feedback from pilot studies shows that the AI-generated content is clear, relevant, and well-aligned with academic goals. The system also aids lecturers in quickly acquiring new knowledge by explaining, translating, and summarizing literature. This paper discusses the design, implementation, benefits, and potential improvements of this AI-driven tool, highlighting its role in modern academic teaching and the associated challenges and ethical considerations.

articleTitle: AI/ML-Enhanced Security Monitoring for 5G-Enabled Big Data Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The integration of 5G technology with sensor network systems has enabled extensive connectivity and data exchange between cyber and physical entities. However, this connectivity brings significant challenges in managing vast amounts of data, including issues related to data duplication, scalability, and security. In this paper, we propose an advanced AI/MLbased algorithm for enhancing the security of 5 G -enabled sensor networks within a big data environment. Our approach leverages both geographical and temporal data to improve the extraction of critical information from multidimensional time-series data, thereby accurately modeling and analyzing attack patterns. The proposed method achieved an overall detection accuracy of $\mathbf{9 3. 3 \%}$, demonstrating a good performance in detecting cyber threats. Additionally, the model exhibited scalability by maintaining high throughput with increasing numbers of sensor nodes. The results ensure the safety, reliability, and scalability of 5G-enabled sensor networks in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Towards an Efficient Navigation Solution for Visually Impaired Individuals: Concepts and Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Due to mobility constraints, visually impaired people suffer from a poor social integration. To address this challenge, the objective of this project is to develop an autonomous and safe navigation solution for visually impaired individuals, guiding them to specific destinations, particularly in unfamiliar environments both indoor and outdoor. The initial focus is on establishing a precise and reliable localization strategy, which serves as a fundamental component for building such a solution. This project aims to address this critical aspect by integrating expertise in the needs of visually impaired individuals and assistive products, localization techniques, signal processing, AI-based algorithms, electronics, and knowledge of mobile network standards.

articleTitle: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Privacy-Preserving Natural Language Interaction with FHIR-Based Electronic Health Records
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Integrating Electronic Health Records (EHRs) into clinical workflows is essential for enhancing healthcare delivery but poses significant challenges, such as improving human-machine interaction through natural language queries. This paper addresses these challenges by leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) within a multi-agent architecture. The aim is to develop a privacy-preserving method enabling clinicians to interact with FHIR-based EHRs using natural language. The novelty of the proposed technique lies in using publicly available LLMs to construct URIs for retrieving FHIR resources and a local LLM to interpret these resources, thus safeguarding patient privacy by preventing direct exposure of sensitive data. Evaluated with the SyntheticMass dataset, the multi-agent system demonstrated superior accuracy and detail over a single-model approach while maintaining competitive response times.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality Interface Quality of Experience Assessment Using Video Game Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Augmented reality is a promising technology, even though it is constrained by hardware limitations. These limitations restrict researchers’ abilities to effectively study AR interfaces. For this reason, many researchers turn to simulations, predominantly using virtual reality. In this position paper, we propose using video games as both inspiration and a medium for simulating AR interfaces. We also present our research methodology for assessing the Quality of Experience of information visualization in geo-located augmented reality through three use cases with video game simulations.

articleTitle: Power Savings of Device-to-Device (D2D) Communication System Using Several Bands 5G Underlaying Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Device-to-device (D2D) communication, in contrast to typical cellular connections, is a direct connection between adjacent mobile users; it skips the base station (BS) and does not rely on network infrastructure to deliver high data rates and minimal battery usage. To address concerns regarding power consumption, D2D connections and cellular networks were combined in underlay mode. Both D2D and cellular connections employ licensed frequency bands in underlay D2D communication; however, due to resource sharing, these bands may overlap, reducing service quality while increasing spectral efficiency. Most existing research focuses solely on energy efficiency (EE) in the setting of individual cells. This article took into account the complete cellular network, including D2D connections across many bands. A closed-form expression for the energy EE of D2D connections underlaid on cellular networks over Nakagami-m fading channels has been derived using stochastic geometric theory, where performance improves by decreasing EE and EE decreases as the density of D2D and cellular users increases. Increasing the shape parameter value m (Nakagami-m order) on the D2D will improve users’ EE is also examined. Results of simulations are used to validate analytical conclusions.

articleTitle: Driver Information System based on Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: In the last decade, rapid advancements in computer technology have significantly impacted various industries, especially the automotive sector. This paper presents a software solution for a system for displaying information about the profile of the driver of the vehicle in front of the ego-vehicle, based on license plate detection (LPD) and recognition. The system consists of two applications, one for detecting vehicle license plates (VLPs) and recognizing text on them, and a web application for displaying driver profile data and reviewing drivers. Various algorithms for LPD and text recognition were explored within this research, whereas YOLOv5 small and PaddleOCR are selected as the most suitable for these tasks, respectively. The experimental results show that the selected YOLOv5 small achieved a precision of 0.9905, recall of 0.9811, and F1 score of 0.9858 for the LPD task while processing 2.69 frames per second (FPS) when tested on an Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8550U CPU @ 1.80 GHz 1.99 GHz processor. Regarding PaddleOCR, the system’s maximum recognition distance for VLPs was determined to be when the vehicle in front of the ego-vehicle is distanced at approximately 8 meters for images with resolution of $1920 \times 1080$ pixels, where PaddleOCR achieved an accuracy of 77.08% after testing. A Django web application was developed to display driver profile data and enable driver reviews based on license plates and the experimental results confirmed its functionality.

articleTitle: Efficient Data Processing Pipelines for Mobility Data Using MongoDB
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The increasing availability of mobility data presents new opportunities and challenges for urban studies and related fields. This paper introduces a data processing pipeline developed to handle large-scale Network Signaling Data (NSD) using MongoDB. Our method addresses key challenges in data preprocessing, such as timestamp compression and noise filtering, to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of mobility pattern analysis. We applied this pipeline to a NSD dataset from Orange Romania, focusing on Cluj County for October 2023. By leveraging MongoDB’s aggregation framework, our approach significantly reduced data size and improved computational efficiency, enabling the extraction of meaningful mobility insights. Our findings highlight the importance of advanced data processing techniques in deriving reliable Origin-Destination matrices and demonstrate the potential for further applications in urban planning and smart city initiatives.

articleTitle: Algorithm for Activating the Alarm System when Leaving the Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: The automotive industry strives to increase the safety of road users using various advanced driver-assistance systems (ADASs). One of the ADAS solutions that should increase the safety of drivers and road users approaching the vehicle from behind is the one that includes an alarm system when the driver leaves the vehicle if there is a possibility of a collision with objects comming from behind. In this paper, a new solution for this purpose is proposed. The solution consists of the YOLOv7 algorithm for detecting traffic participants in video sequences, an algorithm for tracking detected traffic participants, and a distance estimation algorithm needed for calculating the speed of the object coming from behind and the time to potential collision (TTC) with the driver’s door, which potentially triggers the alarm system. After the development and testing of the solution using a PC, the solution is implemented and tested on the Raspberry Pi 4 platform to test its performance in the case of the embedded platform with limited computational resources. The solution has been tested on a custom dataset which consists of 34 different video sequences, aiming to detect five types of objects (car, bus or truck, pedestrian, cyclist and motorcyclist). The solution achieves high performance in terms of alarm activation and is able to process 25 FPS, thus providing real-time operation capabilities.

articleTitle: Furhat PsychScreen Framework: Streamlining Robot-Assisted Psychological Screening Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Initial programming of social robots for psychometric assessments indicates potential reliability and validity in evaluating psychological conditions. However, on average adults express a fair level of satisfaction with robot interaction, and issues like automatic scoring errors and cultural nuances errors were encountered, particularly related to native language biases. Another challenge is simplifying the coding and implementation process for psychologists. The most advanced conversational robot, Furhat, can help addressing these issues with its robust automatic recognition system for multiple languages and open-source programming with human-readable code that enable implementations without advanced programming skills. The study propose a novel software framework to administer psychological screening using the Furhat robot platform, which can adapt to different test formats, question structures and assessment criteria. The framework combines voice administration, via the robot, with a touch screen interface offering a hybrid approach for surveys. The potential impact of the study in clinical psychology involves using social robots to enhance engagement and emotional connection with humans, while also employing automated survey assessments. This approach could uncover fears that might be overlooked by humans or other technologies. Additionally, the study presents results from three test customizations using the designed and developed open-source template for streamlining robot-assisted psychological screening.

articleTitle: Automatically Generated Practice in the Classroom: Exploring Performance and Impact Across Courses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence has been leveraged to develop an automatic question generation (AQG) system that places formative practice questions alongside textbook content in an ereader platform. Engaging with formative practice while reading is a highly effective learning strategy. AQG made it possible to scale this method to thousands of textbooks and millions of students for free. Previous research studies used aggregated data from all questions answered by all students to complete the largest evaluation of the performance metrics for automatically generated questions. However, these studies also indicated that when assigned in a classroom setting, student behavior and question performance metrics would differ. In this study, we evaluate data collected from 19 course sections taught by four faculty members at Iowa State University to gain a broader understanding of how students engage with these AI-generated practice questions when part of their university courses. Implementation strategies for the courses, student engagement, and question performance metrics are analyzed, and implications for further use in higher education classrooms is discussed.

articleTitle: RAG-Aided Approach to Network Experimentation: Case of Wireless Environment Channel Capacity Analysis under Fading and Co-Channel Interference Conditions with Beaulieu-Xie Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: In order to successfully model the wireless channel in the presence of fading, in this work we have taken into account a more recent distribution, called the Beaulieu-Xie (BX) distribution. The BX distribution is able to include several line-of-sight (LOS) and non-LOS (NLOS) components of useful signal, which fact surpasses the successes of well-known distributions such as Rayleigh, Rice, Nakagami-m, etc. BX distribution is described by three physical parameters. Because of this, it is characterized with features of some other fading distributions, including those already listed, which can be obtained from it by setting special values for these three parameters. Beside multipath fading, the co-channel interference (CCI) also disturbs the wireless channels. Using BX distribution, the influence of both, fading and CCI is described. To mitigate these impacts, the selection diversity combining is used. In the situation of an increasing number of users of wireless resources, the channel capacity is one of the most important performance of a wireless system. Therefore, for the described scenario, the channel capacity is determined and graphically displayed. After, the parameters influence is observed for the sake of a successful selection of parameters and better signal propagation conditions. In the second part of the paper, we propose a retrieval augmented generation (RAG) based leveraging large language model (LLM) approach to network design taking free from text (such as network specification, requirements and compliance documents) as input. The proposed approach is evaluated in scenario involving the case of the BX fading and CCI environment.

articleTitle: Validating the OpenBCI Nodes within the Node-RED Library through an EEG-based BCI Application for IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Combining BCI applications with IoT devices and services offers significant benefits in various fields. While there are BCI software platforms currently available, there is a limited number of systems specifically designed to support developers in building BCI applications with IoT devices and services, particularly for users who may be less experienced in programming. To address these challenges, we tested and validated the OpenBCI toolkit utilizing BrainFlow library in the Node-RED platform for visual node-based programming. This was accomplished through a case study focused on controlling a robotic arm with an OpenBCI headset. The research findings indicated that bursts in Event-Related Synchronization in the frequency bands $\theta$ and $\gamma$ in the frontal lobe, and high $\beta$ in the left central and parietal lobes, were particularly significant for controlling a robotic arm through attention and concentration. Additionally, the average threshold for the ‘Mindfulness’ metric, provided by BrainFlow classifiers, was consistent around 0.30 with standard deviation of 0.08.

articleTitle: ConSUMO: Simulation-based tool to evaluate mobile traffic impact on cell towers load
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Due to the rapid proliferation of mobile devices and the integration of advanced communication technologies into vehicular systems, the development of traffic simulation tools is becoming increasingly important in order to help network operators predict and manage mobile service requests load and support informed investment decisions by understanding urban development impacts on cellular network infrastructure. While there exist complex tools that can accurately replicate the details of a real scenario (e.g. Veins frameworks), we have found a lack of more simple and basic tools. Such programs can be useful not only for newcomers to get acquainted with the tools required to perform network analysis but also for more experienced researchers to get a rough estimation before using more onerous methods. We propose ConSUMO, a tool that exploits publicly available data on cellular towers positions and simulations on urban vehicular traffic. It is based on the open-source SUMO simulator and is publicly available on a GitHub repository along with instructions on its use and an example of analysis based on real data.

articleTitle: Creating a Surround View Algorithm with Implementation on a Real Embedded ADAS Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Software, Telecommunications and Computer Networks (SoftCOM)
abstract: Computer Vision (CV) has seen significant advances, and autonomous driving technologies have been transforming the automotive industry in recent years. Autonomous vehicles require robust CV algorithms, while Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) help the driver when driving and increase traffic safety. In this paper, the algorithm for generating a Surround View (SV) of the vehicle is proposed and implemented on a real embedded ADAS platform to test its performance in real hardware scenarios. The algorithm implements geometric operations like image distortion correction, perspective transformation, and image stitching to create a comprehensive and connected surround view. The subjective image quality evaluation results showed that the proposed algorithm achieves a fairly high quality of the final top-view image. The experiments also show that its operating speed when running on a real ADAS platform is suitable for cases when the vehicle speed is not high, such as when parking.

articleTitle: An Efficient Decentralized Fine-grained Access Control for IoT Ecosystems over NDN
